[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Digital Realty is a publicly traded data center real estate investment trust. This session sourced two acquisitions that explain building names appearing across this operators rows in this registry. Per Data Center Dynamics trade press, Digital Realty completed a 7.8 billion dollar all-stock merger with DuPont Fabros Technology on September 15, 2017, adding 12 facilities concentrated in Ashburn, Virginia, which is why several Ashburn buildings in this registry still carry DuPont Fabros own ACC, meaning Ashburn Corporate Campus, naming convention. Separately, per Data Center Knowledge trade press, Digital Realty acquired the East Coast data center operations of AboveNet Inc. on October 2, 2006, for 40 million dollars, including a leased facility at 8100 Boone Boulevard, Vienna, Virginia, which is this registrys 8100 Boone Boulevard row. This specific row, Digital Realty IAD42, Building R, matches a datacenterHawk listing whose own building code and letter exactly match this rows name, giving 22125 Broderick Drive, Northern Virginia.

reading.body:
Digital Realty operates a large distributed campus in Northern Virginia centered in Loudoun County, of which IAD42 Building R at 22125 Broderick Drive in Sterling is one constituent facility. The operator publishes approximately 600 MW of aggregate IT load across this Northern Virginia campus as of 2023, but does not publish a building-specific capacity figure for IAD42. Without a stated power allocation to this building, its scale relative to the campus and to regional AI infrastructure demand cannot be directly determined.

Virginia hosts 326 mapped data center facilities, of which 23 publish power capacity figures totaling 1375.4 MW. Digital Realty's entire Northern Virginia campus ranks 24th by published megawattage in the state, placing it below the largest single published facilities but within the tier of regionally significant operators. IAD42 is one of many named buildings across this dispersed campus, none of which have individual power specifications available.

The facility type and address confirm IAD42 as colocation infrastructure capable of hosting third-party compute workloads, standard for Digital Realty's model. Without published building-level capacity, a power figure for AI accelerators at this location cannot be calculated. Determining whether this specific building matters to AI scaling would require either an operator disclosure of its dedicated IT load, or inference from lease and connectivity announcements not present in published specifications.
